slot.brief: Three resistors in parallel (or series-parallel mix) across a battery; find current in each branch and total power dissipated.

stem: A $2\ \Omega$ resistor is in series with a parallel combination of $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors, across an ideal $12\ \text{V}$ battery. What are the currents through the $2\ \Omega$, $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors, respectively, and the total power dissipated?

verdicts.working: The parallel equivalent is (6×3)/(6+3)=2 Ω, so total resistance is 4 Ω and total current is 12/4=3 A. The parallel branch has 6 V across it, giving currents 1 A through 6 Ω and 2 A through 3 Ω. Total power is 12×3=36 W.

Independent check: The parallel equivalent is (6×3)/(6+3)=2 Ω, so total resistance is 4 Ω and total current is 12/4=3 A. The parallel branch has 6 V across it, giving currents 1 A through 6 Ω and 2 A through 3 Ω. Total power is 12×3=36 W.
solution:
$R_{\parallel}=\dfrac{6\times3}{6+3}=2\,\Omega$, hence $R_{\text{total}}=4\,\Omega$ and $I=\dfrac{12}{4}=3\,\text{A}$.\\
The parallel pair has $V=12-(3)(2)=6\,\text{V}$, so $I_{6\Omega}=1\,\text{A}$ and $I_{3\Omega}=2\,\text{A}$.\\
$P_{\text{total}}=VI=12\times3=36\,\text{W}$.
